title: Token Allocation Workbench: exportable token-cost attribution & interactive drill
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Objective: Design an interactive 'Token Allocation Workbench' in the Redwood Console that enables engineers and finance partners to: 1) slice token-level cost by route/route-parameter (model, prompt template, user cohort), 2) attribute fractional cost to entities (routes, users, teams, feature flags), 3) export reconciliable CSV/NDJSON for billing and chargeback, and 4) surface sampling & aggregation controls to limit volume and preserve performance.

Why this is needed: Customers running high-throughput LLM workloads need actionable cost attribution that ties token consumption to product primitives (routes, prompts, features). Current console views are high-level; this work provides a reproducible exportable ledger and an in-console exploratory surface for debugging anomalies and verifying pricing changes.

Scope & deliverables:
- Canvas view: summary row with total tokens, token-cost (USD), avg cost-per-token, top-10 cost drivers (by token count and USD).
- Attribution panel: interactive treemap + filter bar (time range, model family, prompt template, team, environment). Drill to per-route, then to per-message token breakdown.
- Export: schema for CSV + NDJSON exports with deterministic fields (timestamp, route_id, prompt_template_id, model_variant, tokens_input, tokens_output, token_cost_usd, attribution_shares, request_id, session_id, region). Export options: sampled (1%) or full (subject to retention/quota).
- Sampling controls and privacy: UI to choose deterministic hashing seed for consistent sampled exports (same request_id hashed to same sample decision). Guidance copy for privacy and PII redaction; recommend server-side redaction before export for regulated customers.
- Performance constraints and trade-offs: show in UI estimated rows and bytes for chosen date range & sampling; warn when full export exceeds retention quota.
- Prototype screens: landing canvas, route drill, export config modal, CSV preview.
- Acceptance criteria: design handoff (Figma + tokens), annotated export schema, copy for tooltips and warnings, and a small usability test with two enterprise customers.

Open questions / trade-offs considered:
- Full fidelity vs sampled exports: decided to default to 1% sampled for multi-week ranges with option to request full export via Dedicated/Private contract.
- Attribution model: support both proportional-by-token and weighted-by-cost (where embeddings vs generation tokens weight differently). We designed toolbar toggles to switch and made default 'cost-weighted' for accuracy.
- Row-level identifiers: we include request_id and session_id where available, but add a privacy toggle to drop these for exports shared externally.

Design notes for engineers:
- Backend must provide pre-aggregated slices by (route_id, prompt_template_id, model_variant, hour) to avoid scanning raw logs for interactive drill.
- Export schema must include a checksum and version field to support downstream reconciliation.
- Add a throttled preview endpoint used by the CSV preview to avoid heavy load.

Links to artifacts and references:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/Token-Allocation-Workbench (prototype frames: Canvas 01-05)
- Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Token+Allocation+Workbench+PRD
- Export schema doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/EXAMPLE_EXPORT_SCHEMA
- Related GH issue (backend): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/4281

Design constraints and accessibility:
- Use colorblind-safe palette for treemap and sparklines; provide table fallback with clear numeric deltas and +/- indicators.
- Ensure all export modal controls are keyboard-accessible and screen-reader labeled.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Initial concept review with PM and Eng. PM flagged priority for Q1 billing audits. Action: add deterministic sampling note and export checksum suggestion.
2025-02-12 - Design critique: UX recommended a progressive disclosure pattern for attribution weights instead of a persistent complex toolbar. Revised flows accordingly.
2025-02-14 - Engineering sync: backend team can support hourly pre-aggregates but needs a bounded schema; we agreed on the fields and added a 'schema_version' for forward compatibility. See GH #4281.

2025-02-15 - Privacy review draft: security asked to add export redaction toggle and to mark export endpoints for audit logging. Marked security_review_required=false for initial prototype but noted enterprise exports will require audit hooks.
2025-02-17 - PM feedback: include a 'compare periods' quick toggle (last 7d vs previous 7d) and small-multiples sparklines in the canvas summary. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-02-18 - Ready for stakeholder review: prototype link shared (Figma) and usability test plan drafted. Next: invite two customers for short sessions week of 2025-02-24.
decision_log: Use cost-weighted attribution as default, allow toggle to proportional-token attribution
Default export sampling to 1% for ranges > 7 days; provide full export request flow for enterprise
Pre-aggregate by hour on backend to enable responsive in-console drill
